description: Alert gaps (RFC 0003 §4.3): source gaps moved by each alert kind's offset, only for prayers whose alerts are on, with both observances on a Friday's Dhuhr.

vectors.description: 3 June publishes no Isha, so Isha may fall anywhere from Maghrib (19:00) to the next Fajr (04:11). Isha's alert is unknown in that interval, its 15-minute before-reminder 15 minutes earlier, and its 10-minute after-reminder 10 minutes later.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3 Gaps; RFC 0001 §4.6 missing-event windows; proposal §7.5: an unknown future prayer can make its before-reminder unknown sooner.

vectors.description: The same missing Isha, with no settings for Isha: no alert gap, and the other alerts are unaffected.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3: missing data for a prayer the app doesn't alert never shortens coverage.

vectors.description: No row for 4 June: every kind of the day may fall from its midnight to the 5th's Fajr. The at-time gap lists the five alerted prayers; Fajr's 30-minute before-reminder is unknown from 23:30 on the 3rd.

Friday 5 June publishes no Dhuhr. The source might have declared Jumu'ah, so both settings count: the at-time gaps coincide and merge, and the before-reminder is unknown 10 minutes (ordinary) and 45 minutes (Jumu'ah) before the window.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3 Gaps: .ordinary, and .jumuah too for Dhuhr on a Friday.

vectors.description: A missing sunrise makes no alert gap when sunrise has no alerts.
With a sunrise alert, the missing sunrise is an at-time gap from Fajr to Dhuhr.
The timetable ends on 3 June. Each later day is unknown from its midnight, so the gaps start at the 4th's midnight, and Fajr's 30-minute reminder 30 minutes before it.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3; RFC 0001 §4.6 (unavailable days, one gap per day).

vectors.description: The range ends at 23:00 on 3 June, inside the missing Isha's window: the gaps end at the range's end.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.3: each interval is clipped to the requested range.
